```{r}
## Functions 

#Legend
g_legend <- function(a.gplot) {
  tmp <- ggplot_gtable(ggplot_build(a.gplot))
  leg <- which(sapply(tmp$grobs, function(x) x$name) == "guide-box")
  legend <- tmp$grobs[[leg]]
  return(legend)
}


# Saving figures for AJEV 
W_SINGLE <- 3.5      # single-column width  (inches)
W_DOUBLE <- 7.25     # double-column width  (inches)
DPI_FIG  <- 600      # AJEV: 600 dpi for line art and combination figures
                     # (300 dpi applies only to halftones/photographs, of
                     # which this paper has none). Every figure here is a
                     # chart with text, i.e. combination art.

#' Save a figure as both vector PDF and raster PNG
save_fig <- function(plot, stem, height, width = W_DOUBLE) {
  # "gtable"/"grob" are accepted so figures assembled with grid.arrange() or
  # arrangeGrob() (Figure 1) can be saved through the same path as patchwork
  # figures. bg = "white" is required on BOTH devices: a gtable carries no
  # background of its own, and a patchwork's outer region (where a shared
  # legend sits) is transparent even when each panel's theme_classic() is
  # white. Without it the area behind the legend exports transparent, which
  # can render black in some print/PDF workflows.
  stopifnot(inherits(plot, c("ggplot", "patchwork", "gtable", "grob")),
            is.character(stem))
  ggsave(here::here("figures", paste0(stem, ".pdf")), plot,
         device = cairo_pdf, width = width, height = height,
         bg = "white")
  ggsave(here::here("figures", paste0(stem, ".png")), plot, type = "cairo",
         width = width, height = height, dpi = DPI_FIG,
         bg = "white")
  message(sprintf("saved %s  (%.2f x %.2f in)", stem, width, height))
  invisible(plot)
}
```

# Figure 1
## Figure 1A: Twelve-Day Assay Diversity Screen for Area
```{r}

#Reshape data to combine Size columns into a single column `Size` and create a new column `Size_Rep`
VMB9_combined_area_df <- VMB9_combined_df %>%
  pivot_longer (cols = starts_with("Size"),
               names_to = "Size_Rep",
               values_to = "Size") %>%
  mutate(Size_Rep = gsub("Size ", "", Size_Rep))

VMB9_combined_area_df <- VMB9_combined_area_df %>% rename_at('Size_Rep', ~'Insect_Rep')

# Create a join based on the "Size" column from VMB8_initial_df and "Size Category" from VMB_Sizes
VMB9_combined_area_df_joined <- left_join(VMB9_combined_area_df, VMB_Sizes, by = c("Size" = "Size Category"))

#Save columns in correct format
VMB9_combined_area_df_joined <- VMB9_combined_area_df_joined %>%
  mutate(
    # Convert columns 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6 to factors
    Accession = factor(Accession),
    Rep = factor(Rep),
    Obeserver = factor(Obeserver),
    Time = factor(Time),
    Species  = factor(Species),
    Notes  = factor(Notes),
)

# Compute cage-level initial mean size
cage_initial <- VMB9_combined_area_df_joined %>%
  filter(Time == "Initial") %>%
  group_by(Accession, Rep) %>%
  summarise(InitialMean = mean(Area, na.rm = TRUE))

# Merge into final dataframe
VMB_assay9_Area_df <- VMB9_combined_area_df_joined %>%
  filter(Time == "Final") %>%
  left_join(cage_initial, by = c("Accession", "Rep"))


VMB_assay9_Area_df <- VMB_assay9_Area_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(Area), !is.na(InitialMean)) %>%
  mutate(cageID = droplevels(interaction(Accession, Rep, drop = TRUE)))

#Make Freedom the reference
VMB_assay9_Area_df$Accession <- relevel(VMB_assay9_Area_df$Accession, ref = "Freedom")

# Fit mixed model of area with initial area with Freedom as the reference
model_area_VMB9_initial <- lmer(
  Area ~ InitialMean + Accession + (1 | cageID),
  data = VMB_assay9_Area_df
)

#DHARMa to check model fit
simulateResiduals(model_area_VMB9_initial) %>% plot()


summary(model_area_VMB9_initial)
car::Anova(model_area_VMB9_initial, type = 2)
# Analysis of Deviance Table (Type II Wald chisquare tests)
# 
# Response: Area
#              Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)    
# InitialMean 13.383  1   0.000254 ***
# Accession   55.128 14  8.229e-07 ***
# ---
# Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

  # Results (Initial means): "While cages that began assays with larger mealybugs tended to produce larger mealybugs at the end of tests (χ² = 13.38, p < 0.001), differences in VMB size at the end of tests were detectable even after accounting for initial size. "  
  # Results (Accession): "There was a significant effect of accession on the size of VMB recovered at the end of assays (χ² = 55.13, p < 0.001)... "
  

#Get adjusted means from the LMM
emm <- emmeans(model_area_VMB9_initial, ~ Accession)
emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm)

#Generate compact letter display
cld_out <- cld(emm, adjust = "bonferroni", Letters = base::letters)

letters_df <- cld_out %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(.group = as.character(.group)) %>%
  select(Accession, Letters = .group)

colnames(letters_df)[2] <- "Letters"

VMB_assay9_lmer_df <- left_join(emm_df, letters_df, by = "Accession")

#Add species information for fill colors
species_lookup <- VMB_assay9_Area_df %>%
  distinct(Accession, Species)

VMB_assay9_lmer_df <- left_join(VMB_assay9_lmer_df, species_lookup, by = "Accession")

#Accession levels grouped alphabetically within each Species
VMB_assay9_lmer_df <- VMB_assay9_lmer_df %>%
  arrange(Species, Accession) %>%
  mutate(
    Accession = factor(Accession,
                       levels = unique(Accession))
  )


range(VMB_assay9_lmer_df$emmean)
  # Results: "...and final body area varied approximately two‑fold across the panel, from 1.66 mm² on Barrett Mn‑1 to 3.42 mm² on b 45‑35 M59 (Figure 1A)."


summary(model_area_VMB9_initial)
multcomp::cld(emmeans::emmeans(model_area_VMB9_initial, ~ Accession),
              adjust = "bonferroni", Letters = letters)
# Results: "...only Barrett Mn‑1 (−1.314, p < 0.001) remained significant after Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons."

#Plot adjusted means with letters
VMB_assay9_Final_Area_letters <- ggplot(VMB_assay9_lmer_df, aes(x = Accession, y = emmean, fill = Species)) +
  geom_col(color = "black", width = 0.7) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), width = 0.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Letters, y = upper.CL + 0.3), size = 5) +

    "Rootstock"    = "#476F84FF",
    "M. rotundifolia" = "#72874EFF",
    "V. acerifolia"= "#913914FF",
    "V. aestivalis"= "#585854FF",
    "V. champinii" = "#F0A430FF",
    "V. cinerea"   = "#205F4BFF",
    "V. tiliifolia"= "#800000FF",
    "V. treleasei" = "#F2DD78FF"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "Assay #9: Adjusted VMB Area (12 Days)",
    x = NULL,
    y = expression("Adjusted VMB Area (mm"^2*")")
  ) +

  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle = -45, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5),

VMB_assay9_Final_Area_letters


#Fold-size difference of VMB on Freedom compared to those on Barrett Mn-1?
freedom_SIZE <- emm_df$emmean[emm_df$Accession == "Freedom"]
barrett_SIZE <- emm_df$emmean[emm_df$Accession == "Barrett Mn-1"]

barrett_SIZE /freedom_SIZE
# 0.5581511
#Results: "Specifically, mealybugs recovered from Barrett Mn‑1 were 44% smaller than those recovered from the reference susceptible host Freedom (p < 0.001)."

#Did VMB grow during the course of the assay?
  
     VMB_assay9_Area_cageAVG_df <- VMB9_combined_area_df_joined %>%
  group_by(Accession, Rep, Time) %>%
  summarise(MeanArea = mean(Area, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = Time,
    values_from = MeanArea,
    names_prefix = "",
    values_fill = NA
  ) %>%
  mutate(Growth = Final - Initial)
 
      
VMB9_growth_tests <- VMB_assay9_Area_cageAVG_df %>%
  group_by(Accession) %>%
  summarise(
    p_value = wilcox.test(na.omit(Growth), mu = 0)$p.value,
    avg_growth = mean(Growth, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = sum(!is.na(Growth))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "fdr")
  )

      
VMB9_growth_tests
#Results: "Importantly, cage‑level comparisons of initial and final size showed that mealybugs exhibited growth on all accessions (Wilcoxon signed‑rank tests, all adjusted p < 0.05), confirming that they fed during the assay even on hosts that reduced final size."

```

## Figure 1B: Twelve-Day Assay Diversity Screen for Recovery
```{r}

#Save columns in correct format
VMB9_combined_df <- VMB9_combined_df %>%
  mutate(
    # Convert columns 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6 to factors
    Accession = factor(Accession),
    Rep = factor(Rep),
    Obeserver = factor(Obeserver),
    Time = factor(Time),
    Species  = factor(Species),
    Notes  = factor(Notes),
)

# Filter the data frame based on the "Exp_stop" column
VMB9_Recovery_df <- VMB9_combined_df %>%
  filter(Time == "Final")

# #Make Freedom the first and the control by default
 VMB9_Recovery_df$Accession <- fct_relevel(VMB9_Recovery_df$Accession, "Freedom")
# #check reorder
# levels(VMB9_Recovery_df_sorted$Accession)

#Accession levels grouped alphabetically within each Species
VMB9_Recovery_df <- VMB9_Recovery_df %>%
  arrange(Species, Accession) %>%
  mutate(
    Accession = factor(Accession, 
                       levels = unique(Accession))
  )

VMB9_Recovery_df <- VMB9_Recovery_df %>%
  rename_with(~ gsub(" ", "_", .x)) %>%
  mutate(Total_recovered = rowSums(select(., Size_1:Size_5) != "", na.rm = TRUE))

#Proportion Recovered
VMB9_Recovery_df$Prop_recovered <-(VMB9_Recovery_df$Total_recovered/5)*100

#Remove outliers
VMB9_Recovery_df <- subset(VMB9_Recovery_df, Prop_recovered != 0) 

VMB9_recovery_plot <- ggplot(
  VMB9_Recovery_df,
  aes(x = Accession, y = Prop_recovered, fill = Species)
) + stat_summary( fun = mean, geom = "col", color = "black", width = 0.7, alpha = 0.8 ) +  # Summary bars (mean recovery per accession)
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.2, color = "black") +   # Error bars (mean ± SE)
  geom_jitter(size = 1.5, alpha = 0.9, color = "black", width = 0.25, height = 0 ) + # Raw data points (jittered)
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(       # Species color palette
    "M. rotundifolia" = "#72874EFF",
    "Rootstock"       = "#476F84FF",
    "V. acerifolia"   = "#913914FF",
    "V. aestivalis"   = "#585854FF",
    "V. champinii"    = "#F0A430FF",
    "V. cinerea"      = "#205F4BFF",
    "V. tiliifolia"   = "#800000FF",
    "V. treleasei"    = "#F2DD78FF"
  )) +
   labs(
    title = "Assay #9: VMB Recovery (12-Days)", x = NULL, y = "VMB recovery (%)") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme( axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle = -45, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 1, r = 1, b = 1.5, l = 1, unit = "cm"),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5) ) +
   ylim(0, 100)

VMB9_recovery_plot

# Fit mixed model of recovery with Freedom as the reference for VMB9 (Screen in the `15 accessions)
model_recovery_VMB9 <- glm(
  cbind(Total_recovered, 5 - Total_recovered) ~ Accession, 
  family = binomial,
  data = VMB9_Recovery_df
)

#DHARMa to check model fit
simulateResiduals(model_recovery_VMB9) %>% plot()
summary(model_recovery_VMB9)


emm_rec <- emmeans(model_recovery_VMB9, ~ Accession, type = "response")

emm_rec
#Results: "Estimated marginal means indicated that recovery of VMB during 12-day assays varied modestly among accessions, ranging from 72.5% on Barrett-Mn‑1 to 97.5% on TX2006‑62‑1 (Figure 1B)."


dunnett_df <- contrast(
  emm_rec,
  method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
  ref = "Freedom",
  adjust = "dunnett"
) %>% 
  as.data.frame()

dunnett_df
#Results: "After correction for multiple testing, no accession differed significantly from Freedom (all adjusted p > 0.05)." 

```

## Figure 1C: Higher power experiments merged for growth 
```{r}
#Reduced VMB9 
VMB_assay9_Area_Reduced <- VMB_assay9_Area_df %>%
  filter(Accession %in% c("Barrett Mn-1", "Freedom" ))%>%
  droplevels()

VMB9_clean <- VMB_assay9_Area_Reduced %>%
  select(
    Accession = Accession,
    Rep  = Rep,
    Area      = Area,
    InitialMean = InitialMean
  ) %>%
  mutate(experiment = "VMB9")


#Drop old area
VMB8 <- subset(VMB8, select = -c(Area))

# Size category to area conversion
VMB8 <- VMB8 %>%
  left_join(VMB_Sizes, by = c("Size_chr" = "Size Category")) %>%
  filter(Plant_Name %in% c("Freedom", "Barrett Mn-1")) %>%
  mutate(
    Plant_Name = factor(Plant_Name),
    Plant_Rep  = factor(Plant_Rep),
    Time       = factor(Time),
    Accession = relevel(Plant_Name, ref = "Freedom")
  )%>%
  droplevels()

# Compute cage-level initial means
cage_initial <- VMB8 %>%
  filter(Time == "Initial") %>%
  group_by(Plant_Name, Plant_Rep) %>%
  summarise(InitialMean = mean(Area, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")


# Attach initial means to final rows only
VMB8_final <- VMB8 %>%
  filter(Time == "Final") %>%
  left_join(cage_initial, by = c("Plant_Name", "Plant_Rep")) %>%
  mutate(Accession = relevel(Plant_Name, ref = "Freedom"))


VMB8_clean <- VMB8_final %>%
  filter(Time == "Final") %>%   #Keep only final measurements
  select(
    Accession = Accession,
    Rep  = Plant_Rep,
    Area      = Area,
    InitialMean = InitialMean
  ) %>%
  mutate(experiment = "VMB8")

cages_8_9 <- bind_rows(VMB8_clean, VMB9_clean)


cages_8_9 <- cages_8_9 %>%
  filter(!is.na(Area), !is.na(InitialMean)) %>%
  mutate(cageID = droplevels(interaction(Accession, Rep, drop = TRUE)))

#Create a unique ID for cage
cages_8_9$cageID <- interaction(
  cages_8_9$experiment,
  cages_8_9$Rep,
  cages_8_9$Accession,
  drop = TRUE
)


sum(!is.na(cages_8_9$Area))

#Model for area in VMB9 (Screen of 15 accessions)
m_area_interaction <- lmer(
  Area ~ InitialMean + Accession * experiment + #Experiment included as a fixed effect because there is a significant interaction between accession and test date.
    (1 | cageID),
  data = cages_8_9
)


simulateResiduals(m_area_interaction) %>% plot()
summary(m_area_interaction)
#Results: "While size of VMB entering tests was positively associated with VMB size at end of tests (t = 2.81, p = 0.008), effects of accession on VMB size were detectable even after accounting for initial size."

m_no_init <- update(m_area_interaction, . ~ . - InitialMean)
anova(m_no_init, m_area_interaction)
#Results: "Although the accession × test date interaction was significant (t = –2.20, p = 0.034), including initial VMB size improved model fit (χ² = 7.94, p = 0.005), indicating that experiment‑level differences in starting size contributed to the accession × test date interaction coefficient."

tapply(cages_8_9$InitialMean, cages_8_9$experiment, mean, na.rm = TRUE)


emm_VMB89_area1 <- emmeans(
  m_area_interaction,
  ~ Accession ,
  type = "response"
)

emm_VMB89_area1


emm_VMB89_area1_df <- as.data.frame(emm_VMB89_area1)

#Plotting
ggplot(emm_VMB89_area1_df, aes(x = Accession, y = emmean, fill = Accession)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), width = 0.15) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Freedom" = "#0072B2",
                               "Barrett Mn-1" = "#D55E00")) +
  labs( title = NULL, x = NULL, y = "Predicted final area (mm²)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")


#Pairwise comparison
pairs(emm_VMB89_area1)
#Results: "As observed in the initial diversity screen, the additional 12-day no-choice assays combined with the initial data confirmed that mealybugs developing on Barrett Mn‑1 were 48% smaller than those on Freedom (estimate = −0.95 ± 0.16 SE, p < 0.001, averaged across experiments) (Figure 1C)."

freedom_SIZE2 <- emm_VMB89_area1_df$emmean[emm_VMB89_area1_df$Accession == "Freedom"]
barrett_SIZE2 <- emm_VMB89_area1_df$emmean[emm_VMB89_area1_df$Accession == "Barrett Mn-1"]

barrett_SIZE2 /freedom_SIZE2

1-(barrett_SIZE2 /freedom_SIZE2)
# Results: "As observed in the initial diversity screen, the additional 12-day no-choice assays combined with the initial data confirmed that mealybugs developing on Barrett Mn‑1 were 48% smaller than those on Freedom (estimate = -0.95 ± 0.16 SE, p < 0.001, averaged across test dates) (Figure 1C)."


print(lme4::VarCorr(m_area_interaction), comp = "Variance")
# Results: "Random variation among cages was small for VMB size (cage variance = 0.05 versus a residual variance of 0.74)"
```

## Figure 1D: Higher power experiments merged for recovery 
```{r}
#Fixing issue caused by two columns (Accession and accession). Previously caused drop in cages from 88 to 52.

#Reduced VMB9 
VMB_assay9_Area_Reduced <- VMB_assay9_Area_df %>%
  filter(Accession %in% c("Barrett Mn-1", "Freedom" ))%>%
  droplevels()

VMB9_clean <- VMB_assay9_Area_Reduced %>%
  select(
    Accession = Accession,
    Rep  = Rep,
    Area      = Area,
    InitialMean = InitialMean
  ) %>%
  mutate(experiment = "VMB9")

VMB8_clean <- VMB8_final %>%
  filter(Time == "Final") %>%   # keep only final measurements
  select(
    Accession = Accession,
    Rep  = Plant_Rep,
    Area      = Area,
    InitialMean = InitialMean
  ) %>%
  mutate(experiment = "VMB8")

cages_8_9 <- bind_rows(VMB8_clean, VMB9_clean)


#Update dataframe to work with binomial
baseline <- 5   # baseline of 5 introduced in this assay

cages_8_9_recovery <- cages_8_9 %>%
  group_by(Accession, Rep, experiment) %>%
  summarise(
    survived = sum(!is.na(Area)),
    died     = baseline - survived,
    initial_mean = unique(InitialMean),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

#Create a unique ID for cage
cages_8_9_recovery$cageID <- interaction(
  cages_8_9_recovery$experiment,
  cages_8_9_recovery$Rep,
  cages_8_9_recovery$Accession,
  drop = TRUE
)

#Reduced VMB7 (VMB7 lacks initial size info)
VMB7_final <- VMB7_final %>%
  filter(Plant_name %in% c("Barrett Mn-1", "Freedom" ))%>%
  droplevels()

#Update dataframe to work with binomial
baseline <- 6   # VMB7 has 6 introduced instead of 5.

VMB7_recovery <- VMB7_final %>%
  group_by(Plant_name, Plant_Rep) %>%
  summarise(
    survived = sum(!is.na(Size)),
    died     = baseline - survived,
    accession = unique(Plant_name),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

VMB7_clean <- VMB7_recovery %>%
  select(
    Accession = Plant_name,
    Rep  = Plant_Rep,
    survived      = survived,
    died      = died
  ) %>%
  mutate(experiment = "VMB7")

VMB7_clean$Accession <- as.factor(VMB7_clean$Accession)
VMB7_clean$Rep <- as.factor(VMB7_clean$Rep)

cages_7_8_9_RECOVERY <- bind_rows(
  dplyr::select(cages_8_9_recovery, -dplyr::any_of("accession")),
  VMB7_clean
)

# Ensuring that Accession is in all three experiments (VMB7-VMB9)
stopifnot(
  nrow(cages_7_8_9_RECOVERY) == 88,
  !any(is.na(cages_7_8_9_RECOVERY$Accession)),
  setequal(unique(as.character(cages_7_8_9_RECOVERY$experiment)),
           c("VMB7", "VMB8", "VMB9"))
)
cages_7_8_9_RECOVERY$experiment <- as.factor(cages_7_8_9_RECOVERY$experiment)


#Create a unique ID for cage
cages_7_8_9_RECOVERY$cageID <- interaction(
  cages_7_8_9_RECOVERY$experiment,
  cages_7_8_9_RECOVERY$Rep,
  cages_7_8_9_RECOVERY$Accession,
  drop = TRUE
)


recovery_789 <- cages_7_8_9_RECOVERY |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Accession  = factor(as.character(Accession),
                        levels = c("Freedom", "Barrett Mn-1")),
    experiment = droplevels(factor(experiment)),
    n_total    = survived + died          # 6 for VMB7, 5 for VMB8/VMB9
  )

# Ensuring that Accession is in all three experiments (VMB7-VMB9)
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(recovery_789$Accession),
  !anyNA(recovery_789$experiment),
  all(recovery_789$survived <= recovery_789$n_total),
  dplyr::n_distinct(recovery_789$cageID) == nrow(recovery_789)
)

# Confirm that per-experiment starting VMB count survived merge (VMB7= 6, VMB8= 5, VMB9= 5)
recovery_789 |>
  dplyr::group_by(experiment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cages = dplyr::n(),
                   insects_per_cage = paste(sort(unique(n_total)), collapse = ", "),
                   .groups = "drop")

## Models
#Initial mealybug size not included for recovery b/c it had no sig. association (LRT chi2 = 0.017, df = 1, p = 0.896). Dropping term also allows for VMB7 to be added (adds 36 cages)
m_recovery_null_789 <- lme4::glmer(
  cbind(survived, died) ~ Accession + (1 | cageID),
  family = binomial, data = recovery_789
)

#Model with no interaction term
m_recovery_main_789 <- lme4::glmer(
  cbind(survived, died) ~ Accession + experiment + (1 | cageID),
  family = binomial, data = recovery_789
)

#Model with interaction term
m_recovery_int_789 <- lme4::glmer(
  cbind(survived, died) ~ Accession * experiment + (1 | cageID),
  family = binomial, data = recovery_789
)

# Checking that model used all rows
stopifnot(nobs(m_recovery_main_789) == nrow(recovery_789))

summary(m_recovery_main_789)
anova(m_recovery_null_789, m_recovery_main_789)   # experiment main effect
# Chisq = 29.789, Df = 2, p = 3.4e-07 (baseline recovery differs by run)

anova(m_recovery_main_789, m_recovery_int_789)    # accession x experiment
# Chisq = 0.6803, Df = 2, p = 0.7117  (No effect of experiment)
  # Results: "Recovery of VMB was 41.2% lower on Barrett Mn‑1 than on Freedom (81.2% versus 47.8% recovery; odds ratio 4.73, 95% CI 2.89 to 7.74; z = −6.20, p < 0.001) (Figure 1D) with no accession‑by‑experiment interaction (χ² = 0.68, df = 2, p = 0.71)."

#QC
DHARMa::simulateResiduals(m_recovery_main_789) |> plot()


## Estimates reported in the manuscript

emm_VMB789_recovery <- emmeans::emmeans(m_recovery_main_789, ~ Accession,
                                        type = "response")
emm_VMB789_recovery
#  Accession     prob     SE  df asymp.LCL asymp.UCL
#  Freedom      0.812 0.0318 Inf     0.742     0.867
#  Barrett Mn-1 0.478 0.0436 Inf     0.394     0.563

pairs(emm_VMB789_recovery, infer = TRUE)
 # contrast                 odds.ratio   SE  df asymp.LCL asymp.UCL null z.ratio p.value
 # Freedom / (Barrett Mn-1)       4.73 1.19 Inf      2.89      7.74    1   6.195 <0.0001
    # odds ratio 4.73 (95% CI 2.89-7.74), z = 6.195, p < 0.0001

  # Results: "Recovery of VMB was 41.2% lower on Barrett Mn‑1 than on Freedom (81.2% versus 47.8% recovery; odds ratio 4.73, 95% CI 2.89 to 7.74; z = −6.20, p < 0.001) (Figure 1D) with no accession‑by‑experiment interaction (χ² = 0.68, df = 2, p = 0.71)."

emm_VMB789_recovery_df  <- as.data.frame(emm_VMB789_recovery)
emm_VMB789_recovery_pct <- emm_VMB789_recovery_df |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(prob, SE, asymp.LCL, asymp.UCL), ~ .x * 100))

# Recovery varies across experiments 63.1%-93%. Include a susceptible control in each experiment to compare
emmeans::emmeans(m_recovery_main_789, ~ Accession | experiment,
                 type = "response")

# Freedom: 63.1% (VMB7), 78.1% (VMB8), 93.0% (VMB9)
freedom_RECOVERY <- emm_VMB789_recovery_df$prob[
  emm_VMB789_recovery_df$Accession == "Freedom"]
barrett_RECOVERY <- emm_VMB789_recovery_df$prob[
  emm_VMB789_recovery_df$Accession == "Barrett Mn-1"]

100 * (freedom_RECOVERY - barrett_RECOVERY) / freedom_RECOVERY
    # 41.18545
 # Results: "Recovery of VMB was 41.2% lower on Barrett Mn‑1 than on Freedom (81.2% versus 47.8% recovery; odds ratio 4.73, 95% CI 2.89 to 7.74; z = −6.20, p < 0.001) (Figure 1D) with no accession‑by‑experiment interaction (χ² = 0.68, df = 2, p = 0.71)."

cat(sprintf(
"\n--- FIGURE 1D / recovery ----------------------------------------------
Freedom      : %.1f%%
Barrett Mn-1 : %.1f%%
Reduction    : %.1f%%
Odds ratio   : %.2f
Cages        : %d across %d experiments
Insects      : %d recovered of %d introduced
-----------------------------------------------------------------------\n",
  100 * freedom_RECOVERY, 100 * barrett_RECOVERY,
  100 * (freedom_RECOVERY - barrett_RECOVERY) / freedom_RECOVERY,
```

```{r}
week2_cages <- VMB_Crawler_combined_df %>%
  filter(Week_num == 2) %>%
  group_by(experiment, Plant_Name, subject_id, Rep) %>%
  summarise(
    females = unique(Total_recovered),          # all rows have same female count
    males   = max(replace_na(Males, 0)),        # only one row has male count
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    total = 10,
    unrecovered = total - (females + males)
  )

week2_long <- week2_cages %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(females, males),
    names_to = "Sex",
    values_to = "Recovered"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Sex = factor(Sex, levels = c("females", "males"),
                      labels = c("Female", "Male")),
    unrecovered = total - Recovered
  )


m_sex_host <- glmer(
  cbind(Recovered, unrecovered) ~ 
    Plant_Name * Sex +
    (1 | experiment) +
    (1 | subject_id),
  family = binomial,
  data = week2_long
)

                           (1 | experiment) + (1 | subject_id))

anova(m_sex_host_add, m_sex_host)
```

## Figure 2B: Recovery of females weeks 2:6
```{r}
# Collapse duplicates and compute baseline Week 2 recovery
VMB_Crawler_Full_recovery <- VMB_Crawler_combined_df %>%
  group_by(experiment, Plant_Name, Rep, Week) %>%
  summarise(Total_recovered = unique(Total_recovered), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Week_num = as.numeric(as.character(Week))) %>%
  group_by(experiment, Plant_Name, Rep) %>%
  mutate(
    baseline_week2 = Total_recovered[Week_num == 2][1],
    prop_recovered = Total_recovered / baseline_week2
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(subject_id = interaction(Plant_Name, experiment, Rep, drop = TRUE))


# Remove cages with zero baseline
zero_baseline_ids <- VMB_Crawler_Full_recovery %>%
  filter(Week_num == 2, Total_recovered == 0) %>%
  pull(subject_id)

VMB_surv_clean <- VMB_Crawler_Full_recovery %>%
  filter(!subject_id %in% zero_baseline_ids)


# Build binomial survival dataset
surv_binom <- VMB_surv_clean %>%
  mutate(
    survived = Total_recovered,
    died     = pmax(baseline_week2 - Total_recovered, 0)
  )


# Fit the survival model
m_surv_binom2 <- glmer(
  cbind(survived, died) ~ Plant_Name * Week_num +
    (1 | experiment) +
    (1 | subject_id),
  family = binomial,
  data = surv_binom
)

simulateResiduals(m_surv_binom2) %>% plot()
summary(m_surv_binom2)
# Results:"Using a binomial mixed‑effects model with week treated as a continuous predictor, a significant decline in recovery over time was detected (week effect: z = –4.75, p < 0.001). Since females were not identified at week 0, the model extrapolated the week 0 value, and the accession effect at the intercept was therefore not significant nor meaningful (p = 0.86). However, the strong and significant accession × week interaction (z = –3.74, p < 0.001) showed that recovery trajectories diverged rapidly between hosts." 


emm_discrete <- emmeans(
  m_surv_binom2,
  ~ Plant_Name | Week_num,
  at = list(Week_num = 2:6),
  type = "response"
)

# Pairwise contrasts for significance stars
ct <- pairs(emm_discrete, infer = TRUE)
sct <- summary(ct)

percent_recovery_ci_table <- sct %>%
  mutate(
    Week = as.numeric(as.character(Week_num)),
    stars = case_when(
      p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
      p.value < 0.1   ~ ".",
      TRUE            ~ ""
    )
  )


baseline_df <- surv_binom %>%
  group_by(Plant_Name) %>%
  summarise(baseline_fem = mean(survived + died), .groups = "drop")

smooth_weeks <- seq(2, 6, by = 0.1)

emm_smooth <- emmeans(
  m_surv_binom2,
  specs = c("Plant_Name", "Week_num"),
  at = list(Week_num = smooth_weeks),
  type = "response"
)

emm_smooth_df <- as.data.frame(emm_smooth)

emm_smooth_expanded <- baseline_df %>%
  left_join(emm_smooth_df, by = "Plant_Name") %>%
  mutate(
    predicted_females = prob * baseline_fem,
    lower = asymp.LCL * baseline_fem,
    upper = asymp.UCL * baseline_fem
  )

emm_smooth_plot <- emm_smooth_expanded %>%
  group_by(Plant_Name, Week_num) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_pred = mean(predicted_females),
    lower = mean(lower),
    upper = mean(upper),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


emm_smooth_plot %>% dplyr::filter(Week_num == 6)
# Results: "0.26 females per cage of 10 introduced by week 6 (95% CI 0.12 to 0.51)" and "3.61 (95% CI 3.08 to 3.94)"


star_positions_2B <- emm_smooth_plot %>%
  group_by(Week_num = round(Week_num)) %>%   # round smooth weeks to whole weeks
  summarise(
    ymax = max(upper),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(percent_recovery_ci_table, by = c("Week_num" = "Week")) %>%
  mutate(
    ypos = ymax + 0.5
  )


# Build plot
LCA_Full_Recovery_plot <- ggplot(emm_smooth_plot,
       aes(x = Week_num, y = mean_pred, color = Plant_Name)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper, fill = Plant_Name),
              alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  geom_text(
    data = star_positions_2B,
    aes(x = Week_num, y = ypos, label = stars),
    color = "black",
    size = 6,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
```  

```{r}
# Keep only rows with area (no NAs)
dat_growth <- subset(VMB_Crawler_combined_df, !is.na(Area))

## Model Comparison

#Random effect
m_area_gamma_RE <- gam(
  Area ~ Plant_Name +
    s(Week_num, by = Plant_Name, k = 5) +
    s(experiment, bs = "re") +          # random effect for experiment
    s(subject_id, bs = "re"),           # random effect for cage
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  data = dat_growth,
  method = "REML"
)

# m_area_gamma <- gam(
#   Area ~ Plant_Name +
#     s(Week_num, by = Plant_Name, k = 5) +
#     experiment +   #experiment as a a fixed effect
#     s(subject_id, bs = "re"),   # random intercept for cage
#   family = Gamma(link = "log"),
#   data = dat_growth,
#   method = "REML"
# )
# 
# AIC(m_area_gamma, m_area_gamma_RE)
# anova(m_area_gamma_RE, m_area_gamma, test = "F")


#Check residual distributions

qc_plot <- function(fit, res, main = "Model QC") {
  par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

  # Residuals vs fitted
  plot(fit, res,
       xlab = "Fitted values",
       ylab = "Residuals",
       main = paste(main, "- Residuals vs Fitted"))
  abline(h = 0, col = "red")

  # QQ-plot
  qqnorm(res, main = paste(main, "- QQ Plot"))
  qqline(res, col = "red")

  # Histogram
  hist(res, breaks = 30,
       main = paste(main, "- Residual Histogram"),
       xlab = "Residuals")

  # Autocorrelation (For repeated measures- need to check)
  acf(res, main = paste(main, "- Residual ACF"))
}

gam_obj <- m_area_gamma_RE
res <- resid(gam_obj, type = "deviance")
fit <- fitted(gam_obj)

qc_plot(fit, res, main = "Gamma GAM")
gam.check(gam_obj)
    # Method: REML   Optimizer: outer newton
    # full convergence after 7 iterations.
    # Gradient range [-1.864924e-05,1.687596e-05]
    # (score 957.8665 & scale 0.2472888).
    # Hessian positive definite, eigenvalue range [0.9401091,395.3769].
    # Model rank =  71 / 71 
    # 
    # Basis dimension (k) checking results. Low p-value (k-index<1) may
    # indicate that k is too low, especially if edf is close to k'.
    # 
    #                                       k'   edf k-index p-value    
    # s(Week_num):Plant_NameFreedom       4.00  3.60    0.85  <2e-16 ***
    # s(Week_num):Plant_NameBarrett Mn-1  4.00  3.02    0.85  <2e-16 ***
    # s(experiment)                       3.00  1.94      NA      NA    
    # s(subject_id)                      58.00 40.96      NA      NA    
    # ---
    # Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1


#Testing if growth curves differ overall
summary(m_area_gamma_RE)
#Results: "Using a Gamma distributed generalized additive mixed model (GAMM) with plant specific smooths for time, we found that females reared on Barrett Mn-1 remained consistently smaller than those on Freedom, reflected by a strong negative parametric effect of host accession (estimate = –0.639, t = –6.27, p < 0.001) (Figure 2C)."
#Results: "Both accessions exhibited significant nonlinear changes in body area over time (Freedom: F = 134.8, p < 0.001; Barrett Mn1: F = 55.7, p < 0.001), but the shapes of these curves differed. Mealybugs on Freedom increased rapidly in size, peaking at week 4.5 before declining, consistent with ovisac deposition and the characteristic deflated appearance of ovipositing females described by Sisterson and Uchima (2024)."



anova(m_area_gamma_RE)
emm_area <- emmeans(
  m_area_gamma_RE,
  ~ Plant_Name | Week_num,
  at = list(Week_num = c(2, 3, 4, 5, 6)),
  type = "response"
)

ct_area  <- pairs(emm_area, infer = TRUE)
sct_area <- summary(ct_area)

# Converting Freedom/Barrett Mn-1 to Barrett Mn-1/Freedom
ratio_est  <- 1 / sct_area$ratio
#Results: "Back transformed contrasts indicated that females on Barrett Mn1 reached only 49 to 56% of the predicted body area of females on Freedom across weeks 2 to 6." 

ratio_low  <- 1 / sct_area$upper.CL
ratio_high <- 1 / sct_area$lower.CL

#  Annotation table
area_ci_table <- data.frame(
  Week = as.numeric(as.character(sct_area$Week_num)),
  Barrett_pct_of_Freedom = round(100 * ratio_est, 1),
  lower.CL = round(100 * ratio_low, 1),
  upper.CL = round(100 * ratio_high, 1),
  p_value = signif(sct_area$p.value, 3)
)

# Significance stars for plot
p_to_stars <- function(p) {
  ifelse(p < 0.001, "***",
  ifelse(p < 0.01,  "**",
  ifelse(p < 0.05,  "*",
  ifelse(p < 0.1,   ".",
                    ""))))
}

area_ci_table$stars <- p_to_stars(area_ci_table$p_value)

# Prediction grid for GAMM

  Week_num = seq(min(dat_growth$Week_num), max(dat_growth$Week_num), length = 200),

)

Growth_data$fit   <- pred$fit
Growth_data$upper <- pred$fit + 1.96 * pred$se.fit
Growth_data$lower <- pmax(0, pred$fit - 1.96 * pred$se.fit)

pct_high <- 100 * exp(log_ratio_high)
```

```{r}

# Keep only rows with non-missing Area
dat_growth <- subset(VMB_Crawler_combined_df, !is.na(Area))


df_reproduction <- dat_growth %>%
  mutate(
    # Reproductive status: NA = Growing, 1 = Reproducing
    Egg_mass_recode = ifelse(Egg_mass > 0, 1, NA),

    # Create a factor for plotting
    Reproductive_Status = ifelse(is.na(Egg_mass_recode),
                                 "Growing", "Reproducing"),
    Reproductive_Status = factor(Reproductive_Status,
                                 levels = c("Growing", "Reproducing"))
  )

df_reproduction <- df_reproduction %>%
  filter(Week_num %in% 4:6)%>%
  droplevels()


m_repro_prop <- glmmTMB(
  Reproductive_Status ~ Plant_Name * Week +
    (1 | experiment) + (1 | subject_id),
  family = binomial,
  data = df_reproduction
)

simulateResiduals(m_repro_prop) %>% plot()

summary(m_repro_prop)


emm_repro_prop <- emmeans(
  m_repro_prop,
  ~ Plant_Name | Week,
  type = "response"   # predicted probabilities + CIs
)

emm_repro_prop_df <- as.data.frame(emm_repro_prop)

contrast_repro_prop_df <- contrast(emm_repro_prop, method = "pairwise") %>%
  summary(infer = TRUE) %>%
  as.data.frame()


contrast_repro_prop_df <- contrast_repro_prop_df %>%
  mutate(
    stars = case_when(
      p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE            ~ ""
    )
  )


annot_df <- emm_repro_prop_df %>%
  group_by(Week) %>%
  summarise(y_pos = max(asymp.UCL) + 0.05) %>%
  left_join(contrast_repro_prop_df %>% select(Week, stars), by = "Week")



positionddoge <- position_dodge(width = 0.15)

# Plotting
Survivor_repro_plot <- ggplot(
  emm_repro_prop_df,
  aes(
    x = Week,
    y = prob,

    shape = Plant_Name,
    group = Plant_Name
  )
) +
  geom_line(position = positionddoge, linewidth = 1) +

    aes(ymin = asymp.LCL, ymax = asymp.UCL),

    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +

    position = positionddoge,
    size = 3,

  ) +

  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = acc_palette) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(
```

```{r}
# Reshape data to one row per arena. In a two-choice arena, n_freedom + n_barrett = total recovered. The two plants are complementary ie. this is a paired choice, not two independent samples. Entering both rows double-counts every arena.

VMB_choice$Date <- as.factor(VMB_choice$Date)
VMB_choice$Plant_Name <- as.factor(VMB_choice$Plant_Name)

choice_arena <- VMB_choice |>
  dplyr::filter(Plant_Name == "Freedom") |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    arena     = interaction(Rep, Date, drop = TRUE),  # Rep restarts each date
    Date      = Date,
    n_freedom = Recovered,
    n_barrett = Total_recovered - Recovered,
    n_total   = Total_recovered
  )

# Sanity checks

  all(choice_arena$n_freedom + choice_arena$n_barrett == choice_arena$n_total),
  dplyr::n_distinct(choice_arena$arena) == nrow(choice_arena)
)


# Fitting a beta-binomial rather than binomial b/c arenas vary in preference strength beyond binomial sampling.

  cbind(n_freedom, n_barrett) ~ 1,
```

## Figure 5

# Figure 5A: Power analysis simulation for 12-day growth (body area)
```{r}
# Question: how many cages per accession are needed to detect a given percentage reduction in VMB body area?
# Method: simulate data in which we set the true effect, analyze each simulated dataset the way the real data were analyzed, and count how often the effect is detected.

#Notes: Each power grid is cached as an .rds in results/. Knitting loads the cache; deleting an .rds regenerates that grid from scratch. The cached grids are the ones behind the published Figure 5.


## Shared settings and helpers (used by 5A, 5B and 5C) 
RUN_GATES <- FALSE   # TRUE re-runs the validation gates in all three panels
SEED      <- 123L    # seed used when the published grids were generated

# Load a cached result if it exists. If none, run, save and return it.
cache_or_run <- function(path, expr, seed = SEED) {
  if (file.exists(path)) return(readRDS(path))
  set.seed(seed)
  res <- force(expr)
  dir.create(dirname(path), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  saveRDS(res, path)
  res
}

summarise_power <- function(hits, nsim) {
  k  <- sum(hits, na.rm = TRUE)
  n  <- sum(!is.na(hits))
  ci <- binom::binom.wilson(k, n)
  tibble::tibble(power = k / n, lower = ci$lower, upper = ci$upper,
                 fail_rate = 1 - n / nsim)
}

# Sample size at which power crosses a threshold, by linear interpolation between grid points. Reporting the first grid point above the threshold would overstate the requirement because the grid steps are uneven.
crossing <- function(x, power, target) {
  if (all(power < target)) return(NA_real_)
  i <- which(power >= target)[1]
  if (i == 1) return(x[1])
  stats::approx(power[(i - 1):i], x[(i - 1):i], xout = target)$y
}


# Parameters

NSIM_5A <- 1000

# cages_8_9 (Figure 1D), which keeps rows for insects that were not recovered (Area = NA).
cages_8_9$cageID <- interaction(cages_8_9$experiment, cages_8_9$Rep,
                                cages_8_9$Accession, drop = TRUE)

# Variance components come from a model with the same fixed effects as the analysis model used in the simulation (no accession x experiment term).
m_area_sim_base <- lme4::lmer(
  Area ~ InitialMean + Accession + experiment + (1 | cageID),
  data = cages_8_9
)
VAR_CAGE <- as.numeric(lme4::VarCorr(m_area_sim_base)$cageID)  # 0.07591891
SIGMA_E  <- sigma(m_area_sim_base)                             # 0.8576942

# Fixed-effect values are hard-coded from the reported Figure 1C analysis (m_area_interaction and its marginal means).
B_INITIAL   <- 1.9474   # InitialMean coefficient (m_area_interaction)
MEAN_AREA   <- 1.97     # Freedom marginal mean, mm2 (emm_VMB89_area1)
EXP_SHIFT_A <- 0.4204   # VMB8 to VMB9 shift in mean area (m_area_interaction)

print(tibble::tibble(
  constant    = c("B_INITIAL", "EXP_SHIFT_A", "MEAN_AREA"),
  used        = c(B_INITIAL, EXP_SHIFT_A, MEAN_AREA),
  live_value  = c(lme4::fixef(m_area_interaction)[["InitialMean"]],
                  lme4::fixef(m_area_interaction)[["experimentVMB9"]],
                  emm_VMB89_area1_df$emmean[emm_VMB89_area1_df$Accession == "Freedom"])
))

# Between-run SD of the accession effect: A variance cannot be estimated from two runs, but for two groups whose effects differ by d, the SD of the effects is d / sqrt(2). d = 0.6992 is the accession x experiment coefficient in m_area_interaction.
SIGMA_GE_OBS <- 0.6992 / sqrt(2)   # 0.4944091

# Insects measured per cage, by accession: Not a flat 5 b/c recovery is lower on Barrett Mn-1, so a Barrett cage yields about 2.75 insects against about 4.15 for Freedom. Simulating 5 per cage would inflate power by inventing data that are never collected.
insects_per_cage <- cages_8_9 |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Area)) |>
  dplyr::count(Accession, cageID, name = "n_insects")
N_BY_ACC <- split(insects_per_cage$n_insects, insects_per_cage$Accession)

INIT_VALS <- cages_8_9$InitialMean[!is.na(cages_8_9$InitialMean)]
INIT_MEAN <- mean(INIT_VALS)  #0.3755935


# Effect sizes 
# Percentage reductions in Freedom's mean body area, expressed in mm2 (the scale the model works on). Observed: 48% (1.97 to 1.02 mm2, -0.95).

effect_table_A <- tibble::tibble(reduction_pct = c(20, 30, 40)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(effect_mm2 = -MEAN_AREA * reduction_pct / 100)
effect_table_A
# 20% is -0.394 | 30% is -0.591 | 40% is -0.788


# Design and model builders 

# Data skeleton: which cages exist, their accession and experiment, how many insects each yields (drawn from the accession-specific distribution above), and each cage's starting size (centered, so the intercept is the mean at average starting size).
make_growth_design <- function(reps_per_exp, n_exps) {
  d <- expand.grid(
    rep        = seq_len(reps_per_exp),
    Accession  = factor(c("Freedom", "Barrett Mn-1"),
                        levels = c("Freedom", "Barrett Mn-1")),
    experiment = factor(paste0("E", seq_len(n_exps)))
  )
  d$cageID <- factor(paste(d$experiment, d$Accession, d$rep, sep = "."))

  # One row per measured insect.
  d <- d[rep(seq_len(nrow(d)),
             times = vapply(as.character(d$Accession),
                            function(a) sample(N_BY_ACC[[a]], 1), integer(1))), ]
  d$cageID <- droplevels(d$cageID)

  init <- setNames(sample(INIT_VALS, nlevels(d$cageID), replace = TRUE) - INIT_MEAN,
                   levels(d$cageID))
  d$InitialMean <- init[as.character(d$cageID)]
  d
}

# Fit a model to a placeholder response, then overwrite every parameter with the values we choose. powerSim() simulates new responses from  installed values on this fixed design.

# There is no accession x experiment term here.
build_growth_model <- function(reps_per_exp, n_exps, effect_mm2, seed = 1L) {
  set.seed(seed)                   # fixes design and simulation draws per cell
  d <- make_growth_design(reps_per_exp, n_exps)

  exp_fixed <- seq(0, EXP_SHIFT_A, length.out = n_exps)
  b  <- c(MEAN_AREA, B_INITIAL, effect_mm2)
  nm <- c("(Intercept)", "InitialMean", "AccessionBarrett Mn-1")
  if (n_exps > 1) {
    b  <- c(b, exp_fixed[-1])
    nm <- c(nm, paste0("experimentE", 2:n_exps))
  }

  # Placeholder response, only so lmer has something to fit.
  d$Area <- b[1] + b[2] * d$InitialMean +
            b[3] * (d$Accession == "Barrett Mn-1") +
            exp_fixed[as.integer(d$experiment)] +
            rnorm(nlevels(d$cageID), 0, sqrt(VAR_CAGE))[d$cageID] +
            rnorm(nrow(d), 0, SIGMA_E)

  form <- if (n_exps > 1) Area ~ InitialMean + Accession + experiment + (1 | cageID)
          else            Area ~ InitialMean + Accession + (1 | cageID)
  mod <- suppressWarnings(lme4::lmer(form, data = d))

  # This line prevents coefficients coming out in wrong order
  stopifnot(identical(names(lme4::fixef(mod)), nm))

  fixef(mod)   <- b
  VarCorr(mod) <- list(cageID = VAR_CAGE)
  sigma(mod)   <- SIGMA_E
  mod
}

# Confirm the override took effect.
m_chk_5A <- build_growth_model(reps_per_exp = 10, n_exps = 3, effect_mm2 = -0.591)
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(unname(lme4::fixef(m_chk_5A)["AccessionBarrett Mn-1"]), -0.591,
                   tolerance = 1e-8)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(sigma(m_chk_5A), SIGMA_E, tolerance = 1e-8))
)


# Validation gates 
# Gate 1 (calibration): true effect zero. A correctly specified pipeline rejects at the nominal rate. Expecting 0.03- 0.07.
  #shows the test is not too liberal
# Gate 2 (recovery of a known effect): observed effect (-0.95) on roughly the observed design (2 experiments, 13 cages per accession). Expect power at or very near 1.00
  #shows the test it is not too conservative.

if (RUN_GATES) {
  print(powerSim(build_growth_model(10, 3, effect_mm2 = 0),
                 test = fixed("AccessionBarrett Mn-1", "t"),
                 nsim = 500, progress = FALSE))
  print(powerSim(build_growth_model(13, 2, effect_mm2 = -0.95),
                 test = fixed("AccessionBarrett Mn-1", "t"),
                 nsim = 500, progress = FALSE))
}


# Power grid

design_grid_5A <- expand.grid(
  reps_per_exp = c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 15, 20),
  n_exps       = 3,
  effect_mm2   = effect_table_A$effect_mm2
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cages_per_accession = reps_per_exp * n_exps,
                total_cages         = cages_per_accession * 2)

power_growth <- cache_or_run(
  here::here("results", "power_growth_grid.rds"),
  purrr::pmap_dfr(design_grid_5A, function(reps_per_exp, n_exps, effect_mm2,
                                           cages_per_accession, total_cages) {
    ps <- powerSim(build_growth_model(reps_per_exp, n_exps, effect_mm2),
                   test = fixed("AccessionBarrett Mn-1", "t"),
                   nsim = NSIM_5A, progress = FALSE)
    dplyr::bind_cols(
      tibble::tibble(reps_per_exp, n_exps, effect_mm2, cages_per_accession, total_cages),
      summarise_power(ps$pval < 0.05, nsim = NSIM_5A))
  }))

stopifnot(nrow(power_growth) == nrow(design_grid_5A),
          max(power_growth$fail_rate) == 0)

power_growth <- power_growth |>
  dplyr::mutate(effect_lab = factor(round(effect_mm2, 3), 
                                    levels = round(effect_table_A$effect_mm2, 3),
                                    labels = paste0(effect_table_A$reduction_pct, "%")))

power_growth |>
  dplyr::arrange(effect_lab, cages_per_accession) |>
  dplyr::group_by(effect_lab) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cages_80 = crossing(cages_per_accession, power, 0.80),
                   cages_90 = crossing(cages_per_accession, power, 0.90),
                   .groups = "drop")
# Results (interpolated): "Detecting a 30% reduction in VMB growth required approximately 15 total cages per accession for 80% power and 19 for 90% power across three experiments, whereas detecting a smaller 20% reduction required about 33 cages (Figure 5A)."


# Sensitivity: cost of between-run variation
  # These counts assume the accession effect is consistent across experimental runs (no between-run variation). T The 12-day data show a significant accession x experiment term, so to the extent the effect varies between runs, more cages would be needed. Section below quantifies the cost of that assumption (not discussed in paper)
  # Simulates a TRUE NULL with between-run variation in the accession effect (sigma_ge), analysed without a G x E term. At sigma_ge = 0 the false-positive rate should sit near 0.05; any excess at sigma_ge > 0 is the cost of assuming runs are equivalent. Cached; delete the .rds to regenerate.

simulate_growth_data <- function(reps_per_exp, n_exps, effect_mm2, sigma_ge) {
  d <- make_growth_design(reps_per_exp, n_exps)     # no set.seed here
  exp_fixed <- seq(0, EXP_SHIFT_A, length.out = n_exps)
  ge_lev <- interaction(d$Accession, d$experiment, drop = TRUE)
  u_ge   <- rnorm(nlevels(ge_lev), 0, sigma_ge)
  u_cage <- rnorm(nlevels(d$cageID), 0, sqrt(VAR_CAGE))
  d$Area <- MEAN_AREA + B_INITIAL * d$InitialMean +
            effect_mm2 * (d$Accession == "Barrett Mn-1") +
            exp_fixed[as.integer(d$experiment)] +
            u_ge[ge_lev] + u_cage[d$cageID] +
            rnorm(nrow(d), 0, SIGMA_E)
  d
}

test_growth_once <- function(d) {
  form <- if (nlevels(d$experiment) > 1) Area ~ InitialMean + Accession + experiment + (1 | cageID)
          else                           Area ~ InitialMean + Accession + (1 | cageID)
  fit <- try(lmerTest::lmer(form, data = d), silent = TRUE)
  if (inherits(fit, "try-error")) return(NA)
  p <- summary(fit)$coefficients["AccessionBarrett Mn-1", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  if (is.na(p)) NA else p < 0.05
}

sens_grid_A <- expand.grid(
  cages_per_accession = c(24, 48),       # total, held fixed across n_exps
  n_exps              = c(2, 3, 4),
  sigma_ge            = c(0, SIGMA_GE_OBS / 2, SIGMA_GE_OBS)
) |>
  dplyr::filter(cages_per_accession %% n_exps == 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(reps_per_exp = cages_per_accession / n_exps)

power_growth_sens <- cache_or_run(
  here::here("results", "power_growth_sens.rds"),
  purrr::pmap_dfr(sens_grid_A, function(cages_per_accession, n_exps, sigma_ge,
                                        reps_per_exp) {
    hits <- replicate(500, test_growth_once(
      simulate_growth_data(reps_per_exp, n_exps, 0, sigma_ge)))
    tibble::tibble(cages_per_accession, n_exps, reps_per_exp, sigma_ge,
                   type1 = mean(hits, na.rm = TRUE))
  }),
  seed = 123L)

power_growth_sens |>
  dplyr::select(-reps_per_exp) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = sigma_ge, values_from = type1,
                     names_prefix = "sigmaGE_") |>
  dplyr::arrange(cages_per_accession, n_exps) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

# Figure 5B: Power analysis simulation for 12-day recovery
```{r}
# Question: how many cages per accession are needed to detect a given percentage-point reduction in VMB recovery?
# Design note: the accession x experiment interaction was not significant for recovery so the accession effect is treated as consistent across test dates Experiment is kept as a fixed nuisance effect because baseline recovery differs strongly between runs (p = 3.4e-07). Uses cache_or_run(), summarise_power() and crossing() from the 5A chunk.

# Parameters (from the 88-cage recovery model, Figure 1D)

NSIM_5B <- 1000

stopifnot(exists("m_recovery_main_789"))
vc_cage   <- as.numeric(lme4::VarCorr(m_recovery_main_789)$cageID)   # 0.2689
beta_obs  <- lme4::fixef(m_recovery_main_789)
exp_shift <- c(0, beta_obs[["experimentVMB8"]], beta_obs[["experimentVMB9"]])
# 0, 0.735, 2.055: between-run differences on the logit scale

P_FREEDOM <- 0.812   # Freedom recovery averaged over experiments (emm_VMB789_recovery)
INSECTS   <- 5L      # insects per cage going forward (VMB7 used 6)
N_EXPS    <- 3L

# The first simulated experiment sits at P_FREEDOM (81.2%), and the observed logit-scale shifts are added for the second and third. The simulated runs sit at about 81%, 90% and 97% Freedom recovery, compared with 63%, 78% and 93% observed: 



# Effect sizes 
# Percentage-point reductions from an 81.2% Freedom baseline, converted to a constant shift on the logit scale and applied in every simulated experiment.
# Note: these are percentage-point reductions, not relative ones as for area. 

effect_table <- tibble::tibble(reduction_pp = c(20, 30, 40)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(p_barrett    = P_FREEDOM - reduction_pp / 100,
                logit_effect = qlogis(p_barrett) - qlogis(P_FREEDOM))
effect_table


# Model builder 
# Each insect is a yes/no outcome for recovery in a cage. Its chance of recovery is built from the Freedom baseline, the accession effect (if Barrett), the experiment shift, and a random nudge shared by all insects in the same cage (eg. the plant is healthy or unhealthy compared to other caged plants of the same accession).

build_recovery_model <- function(reps_per_exp, logit_effect,
                                 n_exps = N_EXPS, seed = 1L) {
  d <- expand.grid(
    insect     = seq_len(INSECTS),
    rep        = factor(seq_len(reps_per_exp)),
    experiment = factor(paste0("E", seq_len(n_exps))),
    Accession  = factor(c("Freedom", "Barrett Mn-1"),
                        levels = c("Freedom", "Barrett Mn-1"))
  )
  d$cageID <- factor(paste(d$experiment, d$rep, d$Accession, sep = "."))

  b  <- c(qlogis(P_FREEDOM), logit_effect)
  nm <- c("(Intercept)", "AccessionBarrett Mn-1")
  if (n_exps > 1) {
    b  <- c(b, exp_shift[2:n_exps])
    nm <- c(nm, paste0("experimentE", 2:n_exps))
  }

  # Placeholder binary response so glmer converges. It must not be constant, or glmer stops with "Response is constant".
  set.seed(seed)                   # fixes simulation draws per cell
  lp <- b[1] + b[2] * (d$Accession == "Barrett Mn-1") +
        rnorm(nlevels(d$cageID), 0, sqrt(vc_cage))[d$cageID]
  if (n_exps > 1) for (k in 2:n_exps)
    lp <- lp + b[which(nm == paste0("experimentE", k))] * (d$experiment == paste0("E", k))
  d$recovered <- rbinom(nrow(d), 1L, plogis(lp))

  form <- if (n_exps > 1) recovered ~ Accession + experiment + (1 | cageID)
          else            recovered ~ Accession + (1 | cageID)
  mod <- suppressWarnings(lme4::glmer(
    form, family = binomial, data = d,
    control = lme4::glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", calc.derivs = FALSE)))

  stopifnot(identical(names(lme4::fixef(mod)), nm))
  fixef(mod)   <- b                      # simr's replacement function
  VarCorr(mod) <- list(cageID = vc_cage)
  mod
}

# Confirm the override took effect and the design has the expected size.
m_chk_5B <- build_recovery_model(10, logit_effect = -1.554)
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(unname(lme4::fixef(m_chk_5B)["AccessionBarrett Mn-1"]), -1.554,
                   tolerance = 1e-8)),
  nobs(m_chk_5B) == 10 * N_EXPS * 2 * INSECTS
)

# Fixed Effects:
#           (Intercept)  AccessionBarrett Mn-1           experimentE2           experimentE3  
#                 1.463                 -1.554                  0.735                  2.055 

# Validation gates 
# Gate 1 (calibration): no effect. Expect 0.03 to 0.07.- shows that test isn't too liberal
# Gate 2 (recovery of a known effect): observed effect (-1.554). Expect > 0.95, consistent with the observed z = -6.20.- shows that test isn't too conservative.


if (RUN_GATES) {
  print(powerSim(build_recovery_model(10, logit_effect = 0),
                 test = fixed("AccessionBarrett Mn-1", "z"),
                 nsim = 200, progress = FALSE))
  print(powerSim(build_recovery_model(15, logit_effect = -1.554),
                 test = fixed("AccessionBarrett Mn-1", "z"),
                 nsim = 200, progress = FALSE))
}


# Power grid 

design_grid_5B <- expand.grid(
  cages_per_accession = c(6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36),
  logit_effect        = effect_table$logit_effect
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(reps_per_exp = cages_per_accession / N_EXPS,
                total_cages  = cages_per_accession * 2)

stopifnot(all(design_grid_5B$reps_per_exp %% 1 == 0))

power_recovery <- cache_or_run(
  here::here("results", "power_recovery_grid.rds"),
  purrr::pmap_dfr(design_grid_5B, function(cages_per_accession, logit_effect,
                                           reps_per_exp, total_cages) {
    ps <- powerSim(build_recovery_model(reps_per_exp, logit_effect),
                   test = fixed("AccessionBarrett Mn-1", "z"),
                   nsim = NSIM_5B, progress = FALSE)
    dplyr::bind_cols(
      tibble::tibble(cages_per_accession, logit_effect, reps_per_exp, total_cages),
      summarise_power(ps$pval < 0.05, nsim = NSIM_5B))
  }))

stopifnot(nrow(power_recovery) == nrow(design_grid_5B),
          max(power_recovery$fail_rate) == 0)

power_recovery <- power_recovery |>
  dplyr::mutate(effect_lab = factor(round(logit_effect, 3),
                                    levels = round(effect_table$logit_effect, 3),
                                    labels = paste0(effect_table$reduction_pp, " pp")))

power_recovery |>
  dplyr::arrange(effect_lab, cages_per_accession) |>

  dplyr::summarise(cages_80 = crossing(cages_per_accession, power, 0.80),
                   cages_90 = crossing(cages_per_accession, power, 0.90),

# Note: this study used 88 cages and observed a 33 point reduction.
```

# Figure 5C: Power analysis simulation for two-choice assay
```{r}
# Question: how many arenas are needed to detect a given host preference?

# Note: simr has no beta-binomial family option (what was used for 4C), and the choice assay is overdispersed (phi = 4.52). Using glmmTMB::simulate_new() b/c it generates from the same beta-binomial family used to analyse the real assay. Preference did not differ between test dates (p = 0.335), so arenas are treated as one population and power depends on total arenas.
# Uses cache_or_run(), summarise_power() and crossing() from the 5A chunk.


# Parameters

NSIM_5C <- 1000

# One row per arena (unit of replication). 
choice_arena <- VMB_choice |>
  dplyr::filter(Plant_Name == "Freedom") |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    arena     = interaction(Rep, Date, drop = TRUE),   # Rep restarts each date
    Date      = factor(Date),
    n_freedom = Recovered,
    n_barrett = Total_recovered - Recovered,
    n_total   = Total_recovered                        # insects that settled
  )

stopifnot(
  dplyr::n_distinct(choice_arena$arena) == nrow(choice_arena),
  nrow(choice_arena) == 41,
  all(choice_arena$n_freedom + choice_arena$n_barrett == choice_arena$n_total)
)

# Intercept-only beta-binomial (same specification as m_choice_bb in Figure 4), fitted to harvest the pooled preference and the dispersion.
m_choice_bb_null <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(cbind(n_freedom, n_barrett) ~ 1,
                                     family = glmmTMB::betabinomial,
                                     data = choice_arena)
PHI_OBS   <- sigma(m_choice_bb_null)                                # 4.524407
P_OBS     <- plogis(glmmTMB::fixef(m_choice_bb_null)$cond[[1]])     # 0.6676776
N_DIST_5C <- choice_arena$n_total                                   # 41 values, mean 4.146341

# Between-date SD, used only for the sensitivity analysis. As in 5A, for two groups differing by d, the SD of the group effects is d / sqrt(2) b/c variance couldn't be calculated.
m_choice_bb_date <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(cbind(n_freedom, n_barrett) ~ Date,
                                     family = glmmTMB::betabinomial,
                                     data = choice_arena)
SIGMA_DATE_OBS <- abs(unname(glmmTMB::fixef(m_choice_bb_date)$cond[2])) / sqrt(2)  # 0.278

cat(sprintf(
  "arenas %d | insects %d | preference %.1f%% | phi %.2f | between-date SD %.3f\n",
  nrow(choice_arena), sum(N_DIST_5C), 100 * P_OBS, PHI_OBS, SIGMA_DATE_OBS))


# Effect sizes
# Proportion of settled insects choosing Freedom (susceptible reference), tested against 0.50. Observed: 66.8%.

effect_table_C <- tibble::tibble(preference = c(0.60, 0.65, 0.70, 0.75)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pref_pct = preference * 100,
                fold     = preference / (1 - preference))
effect_table_C
# 0.60 is 1.5-fold | 0.65 is 1.9-fold | 0.70 is 2.3-fold | 0.75 is 3.0-fold

# preference | pref_pct | fold
# 0.60        	60	      1.500000		
# 0.65	        65	      1.857143	<- so Freedom vs. Barrett Mn-1 would be around here	(2.012048 fold difference)
# 0.70	        70	      2.333333		
# 0.75	        75	      3.000000	

# Simulation and analysis 
# simulate_new() takes parameters on internal scales: betadisp is log(phi) and theta is log(SD). It returns success counts, not proportions. Both scales are checked against known answers in the gates below.

simulate_choice_data <- function(total_arenas, preference,
                                 n_dates = 1L, sigma_date = 0) {
  stopifnot(total_arenas %% n_dates == 0)

  newdat <- expand.grid(
    arena_in_date = seq_len(total_arenas / n_dates),
    date_id       = factor(seq_len(n_dates))
  )
  newdat$n_total <- sample(N_DIST_5C, nrow(newdat), replace = TRUE)

  if (sigma_date > 0 && n_dates > 1) {
    form <- ~ 1 + (1 | date_id)
    pars <- list(beta = qlogis(preference), betadisp = log(PHI_OBS),
                 theta = log(sigma_date))
  } else if (sigma_date > 0) {
    # a single date is still one draw from the population of dates
    form <- ~ 1
    pars <- list(beta = qlogis(preference) + rnorm(1, 0, sigma_date),
                 betadisp = log(PHI_OBS))
  } else {
    form <- ~ 1
    pars <- list(beta = qlogis(preference), betadisp = log(PHI_OBS))
  }

  y <- glmmTMB::simulate_new(form, newdata = newdat,
                             family    = glmmTMB::betabinomial,
                             weights   = newdat$n_total,
                             newparams = pars)[[1]]

  newdat$n_freedom <- if (is.matrix(y)) y[, 1] else as.numeric(y)
  newdat$n_barrett <- newdat$n_total - newdat$n_freedom
  stopifnot(all(newdat$n_freedom >= 0),
            all(newdat$n_freedom <= newdat$n_total))
  newdat
}

# Pooled test of departure from 50:50. Quasibinomial rather than beta-binomial because the latter fails to converge at small n inside the loop (NaN SEs and dropped replicates, which bias power upward). The two agree on the real data (p = 0.00077 vs 0.00128).
test_choice_once <- function(dat) {
  fit <- try(glm(cbind(n_freedom, n_barrett) ~ 1, family = quasibinomial,
                 data = dat), silent = TRUE)
  if (inherits(fit, "try-error")) return(NA)
  p <- summary(fit)$coefficients["(Intercept)", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  if (is.na(p)) NA else p < 0.05
}


# Validation gates

if (RUN_GATES) {
  # Gate 1 (fixed-effect and dispersion scales): simulating at the observed preference must reproduce the observed mean and its sampling SD. Expect mean~0.668, SD  ~0.045. Confirmed previously: 0.6681 / 0.0451, which establishes betadisp = log(phi).
  set.seed(1)
  gate1_5C <- replicate(500, {
    d <- simulate_choice_data(41, P_OBS)
    mean(d$n_freedom / d$n_total)
  })
  print(c(target = P_OBS, mean = mean(gate1_5C), sd = sd(gate1_5C)))

  # Gate 2 (random-effect scale, used only by the sensitivity analysis): sigma_date = 0.5 should return a between-date SD near 0.5 on the logit scale. Expect 0.45 to 0.65 (the SD of 3 draws is biased low, while arena sampling noise inflates it). Confirmed previously: 0.548, which establishes theta = log(SD).
  set.seed(2)
  gate2_5C <- replicate(300, {
    d <- simulate_choice_data(60, 0.65, n_dates = 3, sigma_date = 0.5)
    sd(qlogis(tapply(d$n_freedom / d$n_total, d$date_id, mean)))
  })
  print(mean(gate2_5C))

  # Gate 3 (the analysis function on the real data).
  # Expect estimate 0.7376, SE 0.2128, t = 3.47, p = 0.00128.
  print(summary(glm(cbind(n_freedom, n_barrett) ~ 1, family = quasibinomial,
                    data = choice_arena))$coefficients)

  # Gate 4 (calibration): under a true 50:50 null, rejection must sit near
  # 0.05. Expect 0.03 to 0.07 at every arena count.
  set.seed(3)
  print(sapply(c(20, 40, 80), function(n)
    mean(replicate(500, test_choice_once(simulate_choice_data(n, 0.50))),
         na.rm = TRUE)))
}


# Power grid:
design_grid_5C <- expand.grid(total_arenas = seq(10, 100, by = 10),
                              preference   = effect_table_C$preference)

power_choice <- cache_or_run(
  here::here("results", "power_choice_grid.rds"),
  purrr::pmap_dfr(design_grid_5C, function(total_arenas, preference) {
    hits <- replicate(NSIM_5C, test_choice_once(
      simulate_choice_data(total_arenas, preference)))
    dplyr::bind_cols(tibble::tibble(total_arenas, preference),
                     summarise_power(hits, nsim = NSIM_5C))
  }))

stopifnot(nrow(power_choice) == nrow(design_grid_5C),
          max(power_choice$fail_rate) == 0)

power_choice <- power_choice |>
  dplyr::mutate(pref_lab = factor(preference,
                                  levels = effect_table_C$preference,
                                  labels = paste0(effect_table_C$pref_pct, "%")))

power_choice |>
  dplyr::arrange(pref_lab, total_arenas) |>
  dplyr::group_by(pref_lab) |>
  dplyr::summarise(arenas_80 = crossing(total_arenas, power, 0.80),
                   arenas_90 = crossing(total_arenas, power, 0.90),
                   .groups = "drop")

# Results (interpolated): "For the two-choice assay, detecting a moderate host preference (65% of recovered insects settling on the susceptible accession, a 1.9-fold difference) required approximately 36 total arenas for 80% power and 49 for 90% power (Figure 5C). A weaker 60% preference required roughly 75 arenas and did not achieve 90% power within the designs evaluated."

# Context: this study used 41 arenas and observed a 66.8% preference.

# Sensitivity (cost of pooling non-equivalent dates not reported): 
# Simulated under a TRUE NULL with between-date variation, analysed by pooling.

sens_grid_5C <- expand.grid(
  total_arenas = c(30, 60, 90),
  n_dates      = c(1, 2, 3),
  sigma_date   = c(0, SIGMA_DATE_OBS, 2 * SIGMA_DATE_OBS)
) |>
  dplyr::filter(total_arenas %% n_dates == 0)

power_choice_sens <- cache_or_run(
  here::here("results", "power_choice_sens.rds"),
  purrr::pmap_dfr(sens_grid_5C, function(total_arenas, n_dates, sigma_date) {
    hits <- replicate(NSIM_5C, test_choice_once(
      simulate_choice_data(total_arenas, 0.50,
                           n_dates = n_dates, sigma_date = sigma_date)))
    tibble::tibble(total_arenas, n_dates, sigma_date,
                   type1 = mean(hits, na.rm = TRUE))
  }),
  seed = 456L)

power_choice_sens |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = sigma_date, values_from = type1,
                     names_prefix = "sigmaDate_") |>
  print(n = Inf)
```
